doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Evolution of ideas and a planned James Brown jazz album
summary: On evolution of tastes, he plans a third album with James Brown singing pop standards.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: It’s interesting, just to wrap this up, but it seems sometimes your listening tastes and I’m talking generally, sometimes to work backwards, like you know you start out with a certain thing and then you find out where that went — where’d that come from? And where’d that come from?

Well that’s like I said, evolution. You know that’s what happens, the natural evolution of your ideas happens from things that happen before then and before then and before that and before that. You know. So we’ll see what happens in the future. The biggest thing I’m planning for right now is I’m actually already planning my third album. As you know and as I’ve said earlier, James Brown has always been my childhood hero, and it would be the dream of a lifetime to record with James Brown. But I would think how, you know, because it would be too easy to just get a funk band and just do covers. You know that’s too easy. I said well you know James Brown has always said how much jazz has influenced his music. You know people like Jimmy Smith and Horace Silver, Les McCann. So I thought about doing a jazz album with James Brown, and doing like some pop standards. Because even during his heyday in the 60s, he was singing songs like “That’s Life,” “I Want To Be Around,” “Kansas City.” So we’ll see what happens.
